newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian interior troops complete Chechen pullout.
newsitem.headline: Russian interior troops complete Chechen pullout.

text.p: All Russia's Interior Ministry troops have left the rebel region of Chechnya, a top ministry official told RIA news agency on Sunday.

Lieutenant-General Pavel Maslov, chief of staff of the Interior Ministry troops, did not say when the withdrawal, ordered by President Boris Yeltsin, had been completed. It was not immediately clear whether all units of the Defence Ministry had also left the separatist territory.
In November, Yeltsin ordered all Russian troops, both from the defence and interior ministries, to leave Chechnya to clear the way for general elections there scheduled for January 27.
There have been conflicting reports over the deadline for the withdrawal. Maslov said the confusion had been intentional and dictated by the need "to avoid possible provocations".
A spokesman for the Defence Ministry said later by telephone some army units were still in Chechnya.
Tens of thousands of people, mostly civilians, were killed in 21 months of fighting following Yeltsin's decision in December 1994 to use military force to quell Chechnya's independence drive.
